land.text: the Guanabara Bay coast from Rio de Janeiro to Cabo Frio, from which Estacio de Sa 'decisively expelled' the French on 20 January 1567

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps the colony to 1571; the page ends it in January 1567.

capitals.name: Fort Coligny (Serigipe, later Villegagnon island, Rio de Janeiro)
capitals.note: Fort Coligny on the island of Serigipe in Guanabara Bay, built 1555 and destroyed by Mem de Sa on 15 March 1560; the defenders then held the mainland (the village of Henriville) with Tupi help. The page gives no later seat, so the dot stays at the bay.

correction.text: 'took possession of the small island of Serigipe in the Guanabara Bay', where Fort Coligny was built, in front of present-day Rio de Janeiro: the colony at its landing on 1 November 1555

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first shape starts in 1556 but the page dates the landing to 1 November 1555. The island core is a few km2; the 1556 shape (Rio de Janeiro to Cabo Frio) follows.

1556-1563, 10,750 km2 (bbox from about 44.1 W to Cabo Frio at 42.0 W): matches the page's 'coast from Rio de Janeiro to Cabo Frio'. The page gives no infobox area, so no ratio. Fort Coligny fell on 15 March 1560, but the defenders 'escaped to the mainland' and the French and their Tupi allies held the bay's shores until the 20 January 1567 expulsion, so the shape stands to 1563.

correction.text: the shape unchanged for 1564-1565 only: Guanabara Bay coast plus the Florida piece at Fort Caroline on the St. Johns River (founded 22 June 1564, sacked by the Spanish 20 September 1565); the shape must not run on to 1571

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1564-1571 shape (12,370 km2) adds Florida (bbox to 81.3 W, 29.7 N) to the Rio coast. Fort Caroline page: 'Laudonniere founded Fort Caroline on 22 June, 1564' and it 'was sacked by Spanish troops under Pedro Menendez de Aviles on 20 September' 1565. Neither page links Fort Caroline to France Antarctique; Cliopatria's grouping is kept because both were Huguenot-colonial French holdings of the same years. 1566-1567 is the new keyframe below; 1568-1571 has no state (Gourgues burned the fort in April 1568 and did not hold it).

correction.text: the Guanabara Bay coast alone, as in the 1556 shape: Florida lost in September 1565 and the colony expelled from Brazil on 20 January 1567

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the last two years: 'Estacio de Sa founded the city of Rio de Janeiro on 1 March 1565' and 'fought the French for two more years' until 'on 20 January 1567 he imposed final defeat on the French forces and decisively expelled them from Brazil'.

region.text: the small island of Serigipe in the Guanabara Bay, in front of present-day Rio de Janeiro

ledger.note: 1555: Villegaignon plants the French at Guanabara Bay. 'On 1 November 1555 French vice-admiral Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon' with two ships and 200 soldiers and colonists 'took possession of the small island of Serigipe in the Guanabara Bay' and built Fort Coligny. The page names no earlier holder; the land was the Tupi's.

region.text: the coast 'from Rio de Janeiro to Cabo Frio' that the colony controlled

ledger.note: 1556: the French hold the coast from Rio to Cabo Frio. The page states the extent but is silent on the year it was reached; 1556 is Cliopatria's start year, not a page date. The mainland village of Henriville is also undated.

region.text: Fort Coligny and the shores of Guanabara Bay

ledger.note: 1560: Portugal attacks the colony. 'on 15 March 1560, he attacked and destroyed Fort Coligny within three days' (Mem de Sa, 26 warships, 2,000 soldiers); the defenders 'escaped to the mainland' with Tupi help and the fight for the bay lasted until 1567.

region.text: the island fort of Fort Coligny on Serigipe

ledger.note: 1560: Fort Coligny falls. 'on 15 March 1560, he attacked and destroyed Fort Coligny within three days'; the French keep the mainland shore.

region.text: Fort Caroline on the St. Johns River, Florida

ledger.note: 1564: Laudonniere founds Fort Caroline. 'Laudonniere founded Fort Caroline (or Fort de la Caroline) on 22 June, 1564' on the St. Johns River. The page does not call it part of France Antarctique (Cliopatria does) and does not name the earlier holder; Spain claimed La Florida.

region.text: Fort Caroline and the coast to Matanzas Inlet

ledger.note: 1565: Menendez attacks Fort Caroline. 'Fort Caroline was sacked by Spanish troops under Pedro Menendez de Aviles on 20 September.'

region.text: Fort Caroline on the St. Johns River

ledger.note: 1565: Fort Caroline is lost. It was sacked on 20 September; on 29 September 1565 Menendez executed Ribault and several hundred Huguenots at Matanzas Inlet. Dominique de Gourgues burned the fort again in April 1568 and did not hold it.

region.text: Fort Caroline and the coast to Matanzas Inlet

ledger.note: 1565: the Florida fighting ends with the Matanzas executions of 29 September 1565 ('St. Michael's Day').

region.text: the Guanabara Bay coast, from which the French were 'decisively expelled' from Brazil

ledger.note: 1567: the French are expelled. 'on 20 January 1567 he imposed final defeat on the French forces and decisively expelled them from Brazil' (Estacio de Sa, who died about a month later).
1567: the seven-year fight for the bay ends with Estacio de Sa's victory of 20 January.

1567: France Antarctique ends. The page dates the colony's end to January 1567; Cliopatria's last year, 1571, is not on the page (the next French attempt it mentions, France Equinoxiale at Sao Luis, 1612-1615, is a separate colony).

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of France Antarctique
wars.outcome: Portuguese victory: Fort Coligny destroyed 15 March 1560, Rio de Janeiro founded 1 March 1565, the French 'decisively expelled' on 20 January 1567.
wars.note: The page has no article title for the war; the name is descriptive.

wars.name: Spanish destruction of Fort Caroline

zones.text: Fort Caroline on the St. Johns River

wars.outcome: Spanish victory: fort sacked 20 September 1565, Ribault and several hundred Huguenots executed at Matanzas 29 September.
wars.note: Dominique de Gourgues retook and burned the fort in April 1568 and left; no French state resumed.

certainty.note: A fort and a stretch of coast held with Tupi allies; no survey line exists, so both the Guanabara and the Florida holdings are approximate.

sources.title: France Antarctique
sources.note: Identity, founding 1 November 1555, Fort Coligny, the 1560 fall, Rio founded 1565, final expulsion 20 January 1567; no infobox area.

sources.title: Fort Caroline
sources.note: The Florida piece of Cliopatria's 1564 shape: founded 22 June 1564, sacked 20 September 1565, Gourgues in April 1568.

notes: Cliopatria's range 1556..1571 is two to four years late at the start (1 November 1555) and four years long at the end (page: January 1567); the 1564 shape bundles Fort Caroline in Florida, which the pages treat as a separate French settlement (Laudonniere, Ribault) lasting only 1564-1565. A gap-filler may want a separate 'French Florida' dossier; none exists. Capital coordinates for Fort Coligny are the island's position, not on the page. Page budget (1-2) spent: France Antarctique and Fort Caroline. The war name is descriptive. Henriville and the Cabo Frio extent are undated on the page.
